name: South Dakota

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 51st through 62nd Congresses (1889–1913), South Dakota elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: Statehood
events.text: South Dakota became the 40th state on November 2, 1889. Congress gave it 2 seats in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, South Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, South Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, South Dakota's House delegation grew from 2 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, South Dakota's House delegation shrank from 3 to 2 seats.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, South Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, South Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, South Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, South Dakota kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, South Dakota's House delegation shrank from 2 to 1 seat. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, South Dakota kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, South Dakota kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, South Dakota kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, South Dakota kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c063.text: New map drawn after the 1910 census, which raised South Dakota's seats from 2 to 3. It was first used in the 1912 election.

c073.text: New map drawn after the 1930 census, which cut South Dakota's seats from 3 to 2. It was first used in the 1932 election.

c090.text: South Dakota's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1966 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which left South Dakota with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1972 election.

c098.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which cut South Dakota's seats from 2 to 1. It was first used in the 1982 election.
